capture.final_message:
Treat the two outer equivalences as equivalences between propositions that are independently true.

For the character statement, use the averaging projector on \(\operatorname{Hom}_k(W,V)\). Its trace is
\[
|G|^{-1}\sum_{g\in G}\chi_\rho(g)\chi_\sigma(g^{-1}),
\]
while its image is the space of \(G\)-equivariant maps. Schur’s lemma makes this space \(0\)-dimensional unless \(\rho\simeq\sigma\), and \(1\)-dimensional otherwise. Algebraic closedness, irreducibility, and invertibility of \(|G|\) are precisely the assumptions needed here.

Prove the two cardinal statements by choosing fiberwise equivalences from the equal lifted cardinalities, then combining them with the base equivalence: use dependent-sum congruence for \(\Sigma_i f(i)\), and reindex dependent functions along \(e\) together with the fiber equivalences for \(\prod_i f(i)\).

For the affine statement, identify \(s-ᵥs\) with the direction submodule of the nonempty affine subspace \(s\). The affine subspace equals this linear direction exactly when its chosen translate is \(0\), equivalently when \(0\in s\). Nonemptiness also ensures \(0\in s-ᵥs\), which gives the reverse implication from the asserted set equality.

After establishing these four universal facts, each requested `Iff` follows by ignoring its premise and invoking the independently proved opposite side; finally pair the two equivalences.
